'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Assassination of Jovenel Moïse]]
**Former [[Haiti]]an [[First Ladies and Gentlemen of Haiti|First Lady]] [[Martine Moïse]], who was seriously injured during the assassination of her husband, [[Jovenel Moïse]], releases her first public audio statement since the attack. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-57791618 (BBC News)]
**[[Joseph Lambert (Haitian politician)|Joseph Lambert]], the President of the [[Senate (Haiti)|Senate]], is nominated as provisional [[President of Haiti]] by a group of senators, potentially succeeding Jovenel Moïse. [https://www.dw.com/en/haiti-senators-nominate-joseph-lambert-as-president/a-58222978 (DW)]
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**A [[Suicide bombing|suicide]] [[car bomb]]ing in [[Mogadishu]] kills five people and injures nine others. The attack targeted Mogadishu’s police chief, who survived. [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]] claims responsibility for the attack. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/10/mogadishu-police-chief-survives-al-shabab-attack-several-killed (Al Jazeera)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Removal of Confederate monuments and memorials]]
**Two monuments of [[Confederate States of America|Confederate]] [[General officers in the Confederate States Army|generals]] [[Robert E. Lee Monument (Charlottesville, Virginia)|Robert E. Lee]] and [[Thomas Jonathan Jackson (sculpture)|Stonewall Jackson]] are removed from downtown [[Charlottesville, Virginia]], four years after the [[Unite the Right rally|riot that occurred]] in the city. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/robert-e-lee-statue-removed-charlottesville-n1273612 (NBC)]
**Following a short council meeting and vote, the [[Meriwether Lewis and William Clark (sculpture)|Meriwether Lewis and William Clark sculpture]] and the [[George Rogers Clark (sculpture)| George Rogers Clark sculpture]] are also removed from downtown Charlottesville. [https://nypost.com/2021/07/10/charlottesville-takes-down-sacagawea-statue-after-confederate-removals/ (''The New York Post'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*An [[earthquake]] with a [[Moment magnitude scale|magnitude]] of 5.9 M<sub>L</sub> strikes {{Convert|27|km|}} east of [[Rasht District|Rasht]], [[Tajikistan]], killing at least five people and destroying at least 20 houses. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/10/at-least-five-killed-in-tajikistan-quake (Al Jazeera)]
*The [[Miami-Dade County Courthouse]] closes due to safety concerns following the [[Surfside condominium building collapse|collapse]] that occurred at the [[condominium]] in [[Surfside, Florida]]. [https://apnews.com/article/business-lifestyle-health-courts-miami-f2934f1febdb5e82eabe3be2bac0b026 (AP)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 9,353 new cases of [[COVID-19]], thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 827,191. [https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2021/07/10/covid-19-all-time-high-of-9353-cases-recorded-in-one-day (''The Star'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] reports a record for the third consecutive day of 1,378 new cases of COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 166,722. [https://m-en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20210710001000315?section=news (Yonhap News Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] reports a record 91 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|death]]s from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 2,625. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2146543/record-91-covid-deaths-9-326-new-cases (''Bangkok Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]] receives two million doses of the Moderna COVID-19 vaccine from the [[United States]], facilitated through the [[COVAX]] initiative amid an increase in the number of cases of COVID-19 in the country. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/vietnam-receives-2-mln-coronavirus-vaccines-it-tackles-worst-outbreak-2021-07-10/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Georgia (country)|COVID-19 pandemic in Georgia]]
****[[Georgia (country)|Georgia]] receives 43,200 doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|COVID-19 vaccine]] developed by [[AstraZeneca]] and the [[University of Oxford]]. [https://georgianjournal.ge/society/37200-43-200-doses-of-astrazeneca-vaccine-delivered-to-georgia.html (''Georgian Journal'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Moldova]]
****[[Moldova–United States relations]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Moldova]]
*****[[White House Press Secretary]] [[Jen Psaki]] announces that the United States has [[Deployment of COVID-19 vaccines|donated]] 500,000 doses of the [[Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine]] to [[Moldova]]. [[President of Moldova|Moldovan President]] [[Maia Sandu]] praises the United States for the vaccine deployment to the country. [https://www.axios.com/us-donate-500000-johnson-vaccines-moldova-ced56b18-b6cc-483d-ba39-7ec67d604ffe.html (Axios)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]
****The [[Netherlands]] imposes restrictions that require nightclubs and discos to close, prohibits live entertainment in bars and restaurants and requires them to close at midnight, as well as suspending the entry pass program, amid an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases primarily due to the [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant|Delta variant]]. These restrictions will remain in effect until August 13. [https://www.axios.com/netherlands-reimposes-covid-restrictions-delta-f348e2b1-c506-45eb-ba39-e35666cac184.html (Axios)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record 752 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 142,253. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2021/07/10/russia-sets-latest-pandemic-high-for-coronavirus-deaths-a74486 (''The Moscow Times'')]
***[[European Union response to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****The [[European Union]] says that it has secured enough doses to vaccinate 70% of adults. [https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20210710-covid-19-eu-secures-enough-doses-to-vaccinate-70-of-adults (France 24)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in Fiji]]
****The [[Politics of Fiji|Fijian government]] announces that it will soon begin administering the [[Moderna]] [[COVID-19 vaccine]], facilitated through [[UNICEF]] and the [[World Health Organization]]. [https://www.fbcnews.com.fj/news/covid-19/fiji-to-receive-morderna-covid-19-vaccine/ (FBC)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Algeria]]
***Newly-appointed [[Prime Minister of Algeria|Prime Minister]] [[Aymen Benabderrahmane]] tests positive for COVID-19 and will quarantine for seven days. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/07/10/us-algeria-primeminister-coronavirus (Euronews)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Rupganj factory fire]]
**Police in [[Bangladesh]] arrest eight people, including the factory's company owner in connection with the fire that killed at least 52 people. Police say that emergency exits were locked in the building. [https://www.dw.com/en/bangladesh-police-arrest-factory-owner-after-deadly-blaze/a-58226163 (DW)] 
*A four-day [[gun battle]] between security forces and armed gangs in the streets of [[Caracas]], [[Venezuela]], results in the deaths of more than 26 people and the wounding of 40 others. Authorities says that the fighting is now under control, but that there may still be a number of snipers in the streets. The killed people are identified as 22 gang members and four police officers, but a number of civilians also died in the clashes. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-57788117 (BBC News)]
*Police arrest five people in [[Santa Ana de Yusguare]], [[Honduras]], after they were identified as part of the mob of over 600 people who [[lynched]] and killed an [[Italy|Italian]] man accused of murdering a homeless elderly man. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/honduran-police-arrest-five-after-mob-600-lynches-italian-man-2021-07-09/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Politics of Brazil]], [[2021 Brazilian protests]]
**For the first time, a poll shows that a majority of [[Brazilians]] (54%) support moves to open an [[impeachment]] process against [[President of Brazil|President]] [[Jair Bolsonaro]], with 42% opposing, amid graft accusations and a vaccine procurement scandal. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/majority-brazilians-support-impeaching-bolsonaro-poll-shows-2021-07-10/ (Reuters)]
*Protests occur in [[Berlin]] and other cities, organized by exiled activist of the [[People's Mujahedin of Iran]], [[Maryam Rajavi]], to protest the recent election of [[Ebrahim Raisi]] as [[President of Iran]]. Former [[United States Secretary of State|U.S. Secretary of State]] [[Mike Pompeo]] and [[Prime Minister of Slovenia|Slovenian Prime Minister]] [[Janez Janša]] join the protests. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iranian-exiles-protest-demand-prosecution-president-elect-2021-07-10/ (Reuters)]

***The 47th edition of the [[CONMEBOL|South American]] international men's [[association football|football]] competition concludes in the [[Maracanã Stadium]] with [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] beating hosts [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] 1–0 in the final.
